$comment: Which screens the visual suite captures, and which design references are still waiting for one. A reference in `mockups/` that appears in neither list fails the suite by name, so a design cannot arrive and be forgotten. A screen whose status is `baselined` must have a committed baseline and an acceptance record naming the reference it was first reviewed against — that record is what turns 'the console matches the design' from an intention into something the gate holds, because after the first acceptance ordinary visual regression keeps it matched.

accepted.reason: The first screen the toolchain had to prove itself against. It is not one of the designed screens — it renders the run list with no design system behind it — so there is no reference to review it against, and it is expected to be replaced rather than restyled.

mockups.note: The colour token table and its contrast pairs. Baselined by the gallery route the design system introduces, not by a product screen.
Spacing, type and radius scales. Same gallery route.
One investigation, live: transcript, evidence and the decisions waiting on a person.
The empty, error and loading states every surface reuses.
The dark theme. Captured as a second baseline of the same screens with the theme switched, once the shell owns the switch.
